name_reason: Follows data_fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=chapter, descriptor=ch10_end_scene_char_pos_y_table. 'ch10' is the meaningful chapter id (chapter 10), not a Ghidra address residue (0x5211E does not appear in the name). Name reflects data type (table/array) and semantics (per-character Y position). Correct as-is.
purpose: Chapter 10 end-scene (洞窟中的激戰) per-character battle-tile Y coordinates for the 11 staged player characters; the Y half of two parallel 11-byte X/Y placement tables (X @ 0x52113, Y @ 0x5211E).
logic_summary: Read-only const table. fd2_chapter_10_end (the sole reader) copies the 11 bytes one at a time onto an on-stack block, then loops i=0..0xA storing block[i] into runtime_char[i].bPos_y (a single-byte field). No struct stride, no wider element access, no sign extension. Sprite facing is an inline constant (2) in the caller, so there is no separate facing table.
element_semantics: Each entry = battle-tile Y coordinate (uint8) for one of the 11 staged player characters; values are small tile coords 38..40 (0x26..0x28). Index = character slot 0..10.
notes: Memory @ 0x5211E = [38,39,38,38,39,38,39,39,40,40,40], byte-identical to the C source array. xrefs: only fd2_chapter_10_end (READ @ 0x2361E, DATA @ 0x23619); no writers -> const confirmed by game-side write-xref absence. Existing src comment block (chtab.c lines 483-504) already accurate/precise and matches the decompile, so kept verbatim (no Edit to src). Ghidra data plate was empty/null, so created a concise plate (run_script_inline + cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,...)) reflecting the src conclusion, then save_program() succeeded. Plate retains the Chinese chapter name like the caller's plate (Ghidra plates allow CJK; ASCII-only rule applies to src/ code text).
